crops.name: Citrus (Sweet Orange / Lime)
crops.scientificName: Citrus spp. (e.g. Citrus sinensis — sweet orange, Citrus aurantiifolia — acid lime)

conditions.name: Panama Wilt / Fusarium Wilt
keySymptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves starting at the leaf margin and advancing inward.
Leaves collapse at petiole junction and hang down skirt-like around pseudostem.

conditions.name: Fruit Cracking (Physiological)
keySymptoms: Irregular cracks or splits on the fruit skin, often radiating outward from near the stalk/calyx end.
Cracks may heal over with a corky, hardened edge, or stay open and invite secondary soft rot.

conditions.name: Phomopsis Blight & Fruit Rot
keySymptoms: Small circular brown spots with greyish centers on leaves, which can enlarge and merge, causing leaf drop.
A girdling blight near the soil line can kill young seedlings (damping-off) in the nursery.

conditions.name: Shoot and Fruit Borer
keySymptoms: Young shoots wilt and droop ("dead heart") with a small bore hole and larval frass (excreta) visible at the entry point.
In fruits, a small bore hole plugged with frass is visible on the surface; the fruit shows little external rot but is hollowed and tunneled…

conditions.name: Wet Fruit Rot
keySymptoms: A soft, watery rot that spreads rapidly across the fruit, often starting where the fruit touches wet soil or has an injury (including an ol…
The fruit becomes mushy with a distinct foul smell; whitish or grey fungal growth can appear on the surface in advanced stages.

conditions.name: Anthracnose / Fruit Rot
keySymptoms: Sunken, circular to oval spots on ripening and ripe fruit, often with visible concentric rings within the lesion.
As the spot matures, tiny orange-to-pink spore masses appear in the center, especially in humid weather — a distinguishing feature of this…

conditions.name: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus
keySymptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and crinkling of leaf margins.
Vein clearing, thickening, and brittle leathery leaves.

conditions.name: Powdery Mildew
keySymptoms: Pale yellow, diffuse patches appear on the upper leaf surface, with a fine white to greyish powdery fungal growth visible on the correspond…
Older, lower leaves are usually affected first, turning yellow, then brown, and dropping prematurely as the disease progresses.

conditions.name: Chilli Thrips / Murda Complex
keySymptoms: Upward curling of young leaves with silvery or bronze streaking and scarring along the undersides, concentrated near growing tips.
Stunted, bushy, deformed new growth ("Murda"/malformation) with shortened internodes.

conditions.name: Citrus Black Spot
keySymptoms: "Hard spot" on mature fruit: small, circular lesions with a grey-brown necrotic center and a dark margin, often with tiny black dots (pycni…
"Virulent/false melanose spot" on still-green fruit: irregular, spreading dark lesions that can cover a larger area of the rind.

conditions.name: Citrus Canker
keySymptoms: Raised, corky, crater-like ("volcano-shaped") lesions on leaves, twigs, and fruit, each typically surrounded by a yellow, water-soaked-look…
Lesions often cluster along leaf margins and areas prone to wind/thorn injury, where the bacteria enter through wounds or natural openings.

conditions.name: Citrus Greening (Huanglongbing / HLB)
keySymptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellow mottling on leaves — the pattern does NOT mirror across the midrib/leaf center, unlike most nutrient deficiencie…
Yellowing often appears sector-by-sector on the tree (one or a few branches affected while others look normal), sometimes called "yellow sh…

conditions.name: Melanose
keySymptoms: Small, raised, corky brown pustules with a rough, "sandpaper"-like texture on leaves, twigs, and fruit rind — usually more a cosmetic issue…
On fruit, rain-splashed spores running down the surface can leave a distinctive "tear-streak" or "mudcake" pattern of raised brown specks.

conditions.name: Citrus Scab
keySymptoms: Wart-like, raised, irregular corky scabby outgrowths on young leaves, twigs, and fruit, often pointed or conical rather than flat.
Mainly affects very young, actively growing (flush) tissue; heavily affected young leaves can become twisted or distorted as they expand ar…

conditions.name: Bacterial Blight (Angular Leaf Spot / Black Arm)
keySymptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular lesions on leaves, bound by the leaf veins (giving an "angular" shape rather than round), which dry to dark br…
On stems and branches, elongated black streaks or lesions can appear and, in severe cases, girdle the stem — a phase often called "black ar…

conditions.name: Pink Bollworm
keySymptoms: Rosetted flowers ("rosette blooms") that fail to open normally.
Prematurely opened bolls with stained, poor quality lint.

conditions.name: Cotton Jassids (Leafhoppers)
keySymptoms: Leaf margins turn yellow and curl downward (cupping) early on, usually noticed first on the lower/older leaves.
As feeding continues, the yellowing progresses to a reddish-bronze discoloration spreading inward from the margins — a symptom pattern ofte…

conditions.name: Cotton Whitefly
keySymptoms: Clouds of small white adult insects flying up when the plant canopy is disturbed; nymphs visible as tiny flat scales on leaf undersides.
Sticky honeydew excretion on leaves leading to black sooty mould growth, reducing photosynthesis.

conditions.name: Bud Necrosis Disease (PBNV)
keySymptoms: The central growing point (terminal bud) turns brown-black and dies — the symptom that gives this disease its name.
Young leaves show chlorotic and necrotic ring spots or mottled patterns before the bud dies.

conditions.name: Collar Rot (Seedling Blight)
keySymptoms: Young seedlings wilt and collapse within 2-3 weeks of sowing, often before or just after emergence.
A girdling lesion forms at the collar region (stem base, right at the soil line); peeling back the soil there reveals a sooty black, powder…

conditions.name: Groundnut Rust
keySymptoms: Small, raised, orange to reddish-brown pustules (uredinia) on the lower leaf surface, which rupture and release a dusty orange spore mass t…
Corresponding pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface directly above each pustule.

conditions.name: Tikka Leaf Spot
keySymptoms: Early leaf spot: Circular reddish-brown to dark brown spots surrounded by a prominent yellow halo on upper leaf surface.
Late leaf spot: Nearly circular dark black spots mostly on lower leaf surface without a distinct yellow halo.

conditions.name: Fall Armyworm
keySymptoms: Pinholes and ragged "window-pane" feeding marks on young leaves.
Heavy sawdust-like fecal frass accumulation inside the leaf whorl.

conditions.name: Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight
keySymptoms: Irregular, water-soaked, grayish-brown lesions with a concentric banded (zonate) pattern appear first on the leaf sheath near the base, the…
Lesions coalesce into large necrotic patches that can girdle the leaf sheath and stalk, causing affected leaves to dry up starting from low…

conditions.name: Spotted Stem Borer
keySymptoms: Rows of small, neat pinhole perforations across young leaves as the newly hatched larva feeds while still on the leaf surface before boring…
Larvae bore into the central shoot/stem, producing a "deadheart" — the central whorl turns brown, dries up, and can be pulled out easily wi…

conditions.name: Turcicum Leaf Blight
keySymptoms: Long, elliptical, cigar-shaped (boat-shaped) grayish-green to tan lesions on leaves, typically starting on lower leaves first.
Lesions enlarge and run parallel to leaf veins, often coalescing to blight large sections of the leaf.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
keySymptoms: Dark brown to black speckling on panicles/blossoms causing blossom blight and flower drop.
Irregular dark brown leaf spots with necrotic centers.

conditions.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
keySymptoms: Circular to irregular brown spots, often with visible concentric rings ("target" or "bullseye" pattern), surrounded by a yellow halo.
Spots are typically larger (up to 1-2 cm) than other okra leaf spots and start on the older, lower leaves first.

conditions.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot
keySymptoms: Small to medium, roughly circular to angular grayish-brown spots on both leaf surfaces, often bound by the leaf veins.
Spots have a distinct reddish-brown to purplish margin and a dry, slightly grainy-looking center, without the concentric rings seen in Alte…

conditions.name: Downy Mildew
keySymptoms: Pale yellow, angular patches on the upper leaf surface, bounded by the leaf veins (a checkerboard-like pattern).
A greyish-white to faintly purplish, fuzzy (downy) fungal growth appears on the corresponding underside of the leaf, most visible in early…

conditions.name: Yellow Vein Mosaic / Leaf Curl Virus
keySymptoms: Veins on young leaves turn yellow first, forming a clear yellow network pattern while the tissue between veins stays green (vein-clearing/n…
As it progresses, the whole leaf may turn yellow, thicken, and curl upward; plants become visibly stunted with shortened internodes.

conditions.name: Phyllosticta Leaf Spot
keySymptoms: Small (pinhead to about 5mm) circular spots with a pale grayish-white center and a sharply defined dark brown margin.
Under close inspection, tiny black dots (pycnidia, the fungus's fruiting bodies) are often visible scattered within the pale center of olde…

conditions.name: Rice Blast
keySymptoms: Spindle-shaped (eye-shaped) lesions on leaf blades with pointed ends.
Lesion center turns ash-gray or whitish; margins turn dark brown or reddish-brown.

conditions.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
keySymptoms: Water-soaked pale stripes begin at the leaf tip or along one margin and extend downwards.
Stripes turn straw-yellow then greyish-white, with a wavy or rippled edge rather than a sharp border.

conditions.name: Brown Planthopper (Hopperburn)
keySymptoms: Circular patches of plants turning orange-brown and drying up ("hopperburn"), typically starting at a low-lying spot or where planting is d…
Parting the base of tillers in or near a hopperburn patch reveals clusters of brown, wedge-shaped adult and nymph insects feeding at the st…

conditions.name: Brown Spot
keySymptoms: Many small, separate, circular to oval brown spots scattered evenly over the leaf blade.
Mature spots have a dark brown margin and a grey or pale tan centre, roughly the size and shape of a sesame seed.

conditions.name: False Smut
keySymptoms: Individual grains within the panicle (ear head) are replaced by large velvety spore balls, much bigger than a normal rice grain, ranging fr…
Spore balls burst through and enlarge beyond the husk, becoming clearly visible after flowering, usually scattered among otherwise normal-l…

conditions.name: Rice Gall Midge
keySymptoms: The affected tiller turns into a hollow, silvery-white tube resembling an onion leaf — the characteristic silver shoot or onion shoot.
The tube is pale, elongated, and produces no panicle at all.

conditions.name: Rice Leaf Folder
keySymptoms: Leaf blades folded or rolled longitudinally and webbed shut with fine silk threads, forming a tube-like shelter the caterpillar feeds insid…
Unfolding an affected leaf reveals long, white to transparent parallel streaks where the caterpillar has scraped away the green tissue from…

conditions.name: Sheath Blight
keySymptoms: Oval, greenish-grey water-soaked blotches on the leaf sheath, starting near the water line.
Lesions dry to a straw-white centre ringed by an irregular purple-brown border, giving a snakeskin pattern.

conditions.name: Yellow Stem Borer
keySymptoms: Dead heart in the vegetative stage: the central shoot dries to straw colour while the surrounding leaves stay green, and it pulls out easil…
White ear in the reproductive stage: the whole panicle emerges white, erect and empty, with no filled grain.

conditions.name: Zinc Deficiency (Khaira)
keySymptoms: Appears two to four weeks after transplanting, usually in distinct patches rather than evenly across the field.
Dusty rust-brown blotches develop on the lower leaves, starting near the leaf base and midrib.

conditions.name: Red Rot
keySymptoms: Discoloration and drying of upper leaves/crown.
Reddening of internal stalk pith with characteristic white cross-bands when cane is split longitudinally.

conditions.name: Early Blight
keySymptoms: Concentric dark brown circular rings (target-board appearance) on older lower leaves.
Yellowing of foliage surrounding concentric lesions followed by leaf drop.

conditions.name: Turmeric Leaf Spot
keySymptoms: Small, oval to irregular dark brown spots with a yellow halo, scattered across the leaf blade (distinct from the many small rectangular spo…
Spots may enlarge and coalesce under heavy infection, giving leaves a blighted, scorched appearance.

conditions.name: Rhizome Rot
keySymptoms: Water-soaked lesions at collar region of pseudostem near ground level.
Leaves turn pale yellow and dry up from tips downward along margins.
